feature: Design study pages stop borrowing design system class names
summary: Every page rule that styles a design system class name has been judged by hand: ten were page-local boxes wearing a component's name and are renamed, the rest refine the real component. The loudest fix is the fake app window in six video walkthroughs, which was inheriting a fixed 420px width and running off the right edge of its frame.
setup: Design dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791, any page under /pages. No app build involved.

try.do: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/video-cut-wt.html and look at the small app window inside the preview frame. It now has the same margin on both sides.
Compare with how it looked before: the window ran into the frame's right edge and lost its margin.
Switch the system to light mode and reload. The margins hold.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/lang-elevation.html and scroll to Live examples. The Layers list (Card, Headline, Button) sits as a tight list of rows instead of spaced out by an inherited margin.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/image.html and find the mask row that says EDITING. It is now the design system's own row tag rather than a hand-drawn copy.
From docs/design/mocks run: node shared/check-reserved.mjs. It reports 86 guarded names and passes. Add --pairs to see the full triage shortlist.

evaluate: In the video walkthroughs, does the preview window now sit centred in its frame the way the mock intended, or did the fixed width give it a proportion you preferred?
On the elevation page, is the tighter Layers list right, or did the old spacing read better in that small scene?
On the image page, the EDITING tag lost its thin outline when it became the shared row tag. Is the shared look acceptable there?
Is the write-up in shared/RESERVED-TRIAGE.md the kind of record you would want the next agent to read before naming a page class?
rough: The gate still cannot tell a refinement from a borrowing in general; it now catches fixed widths on top of grids, floats and absolute position, and the rest stays a human judgment recorded in RESERVED-TRIAGE.md.

The elevation page's 'glass titlebar · elev 2' annotation still sits on top of the window title in the Live examples scene. That is the already filed task an-elevation-annotation-covers-the-window-title, not touched here.

The video walkthrough preview also lost a heavy 40px drop shadow it had been inheriting. It looks flatter and, I think, more like a window inside a recording, but it is a visible change you did not ask for.
